record.paper_title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems
record.context_brief: Standard QA framework for safety-critical ML
record.original_question: How can a common, socially accepted quality-assurance framework be established for safety-critical machine-learning systems, such as automated-driving systems that rely on machine-learning or deep-learning models for environmental perception and decision-making, when there are not yet widely accepted quality-assurance concepts and techniques and when the relevant open problems must be organized across automobile standardization, statistics, software engineering, machine learning, and theoretical computer science?

evidence.quote: Quality assurance frameworks are required for such machine-learning systems, but there are no widely accepted and established quality-assurance concepts and techniques. At the same time, open problems and the relevant technical fields are not organized.

Experts from each specialized field as mentioned in this paper should gather together, create technically reasonable drafts, proposing QA processes, and form consensus (standardization) overviewing the worldwide trends of safety-critical machine-learning systems.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem of establishing a unified, socially accepted QA framework for safety-critical ML systems remains open. While related standards have advanced (e.g., ISO 21448 SOTIF, ISO/PAS 8800 on AI in road vehicles published in 2024, ISO/IEC TR 5469 on functional safety and AI, and UL 4600), no single, internationally consensus-adopted QA framework spanning all five fields exists, and active research and standardization continue.

status_evidence.title: ISO/PAS 8800:2024 Road vehicles — Safety and artificial intelligence
status_evidence.snippet: Specifies safety-related properties and risk factors for AI systems used in road vehicles; published 2024 as a publicly available specification, not yet a fully consensus international standard.
status_evidence.claim: Standardization of QA for ML in automated driving is in progress but not finalized as a universally accepted framework.

status_evidence.title: ISO/IEC TR 5469:2024 Artificial intelligence — Functional safety and AI systems
status_evidence.snippet: Technical report describing properties, related risk factors, available methods and processes relating to use of AI inside safety-related functions; remains a TR rather than a normative consensus standard.
status_evidence.claim: International QA concepts for safety-critical AI exist as technical reports but are not yet established consensus frameworks.

status_evidence.title: UL 4600 Standard for Safety for the Evaluation of Autonomous Products
status_evidence.snippet: Goal/claim-based safety case standard for autonomous systems; one of several competing approaches with no global consensus.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing QA approaches indicate the unified framework problem is still open.
